name: Hotel Bel-Air
positioning: Dorchester Collection hotel in Bel Air, Los Angeles, set within 12 acres of landscaped gardens a mile west of Beverly Hills
best_for: Travelers who want a secluded garden setting close to Beverly Hills
Guests interested in the hotel's Hollywood history
Guests travelling with a small dog

facts.text: The hotel is at 701 Stone Canyon Road in Bel Air, Los Angeles, a mile west of Beverly Hills and half a mile from Sunset Boulevard.
The estate is set within 12 acres of landscaped gardens.
483 specimen trees and more than 4,000 plants surround the paths through the hotel grounds.
The hotel is designed in a Spanish Colonial style.
Room interiors are by Alexandra Champalimaud.
The Restaurant at Hotel Bel-Air serves modern Californian cuisine with a Mediterranean influence.
Norman Seeff's photographs of figures such as Cher, Tina Turner and Steve Jobs line the walls of the Bar & Lounge.
The Bar & Lounge has live music every evening.
The spa has seven treatment rooms, a private enclave, a nail suite and steam rooms.
The spa offers Valmont facials made with Swiss ingredients.
Hotel guests have 24-hour access to the fitness studio.
Up to two small dogs per room are welcome for a fee, with a bowl, bed and treats provided.

highlights.text: Instead of long corridors, most rooms and suites open directly onto the gardens.
The pool area was once a horse-riding ring, transformed by owner Joseph Drown in the 1940s.
The Restaurant still serves the tortilla soup that debuted there in 1980.
The Canyon Studio has retractable walls opening onto a large private patio with a fireplace and spa pool.
The opening sequence of the 1965 film The Silencers shows Dean Martin beside the hotel pool.

considerations.text: The hotel sits in an exclusive gated community removed from the bustle of Los Angeles; the airport and the beach are each around 30 to 40 minutes away.
Breakfast is not automatically included in the room rate.
The pool is reserved for hotel guests, and children under 16 must be accompanied by a parent or guardian.

sources.title: Conde Nast Traveler: Hotel Bel-Air, Dorchester Collection
